title: COBRA - binary Transformer accelerator on FPGA with 1-bit multiplier
problem: Transformer inference on edge devices faces power and area constraints. Standard floating-point multiplications consume significant energy, limiting deployment on resource-constrained platforms.
motivation: Binarized neural networks with 1-bit multipliers can dramatically reduce area and power while maintaining competitive accuracy, enabling efficient Transformer deployment on FPGAs.
method: COBRA builds a specialized hardware accelerator (using programmable FPGA chips) that runs Transformer models by representing weights and activations as 1-bit values (either 0 or 1 instead of full numbers). This representation converts multiplication operations into much simpler binary logic gates (AND and XOR operations), which require far less energy and silicon area. The FPGA design is optimized to maximize prediction throughput while keeping energy consumption low for edge device deployment.
key_novelty: COBRA's core idea is using 1-bit multiplications in an FPGA-based Transformer to reduce energy use for edge device inference.
contributions: 311× energy efficiency improvement over GPU baseline
Practical FPGA deployment methodology for binary Transformers
limitations: 1-bit quantization may introduce significant accuracy loss for certain Transformer tasks, and the approach requires specialized quantization-aware training.
